newsitem.title: FRANCE: Three hikers die in accidents in French Alps.
newsitem.headline: Three hikers die in accidents in French Alps.

text.p: Three hikers fell to their deaths in three separate accidents in the French Alps on Thursday, raising the death toll in the mountainous region in recent days to 20, police said.

A 37-year-old Parisian died in a fall while hiking on a footpath at an altitude of 1,800 metres (5,850 ft) in the central Alps, and a resident of Marseille in his 70s and an unidentified hiker plunged to their deaths while walking on mountain ridges east of the northern Alpine town of Annecy.
Warm, sunny weather has caused a surge in the number of climbers and hikers in the Alps, with some risking tougher routes to flee the summer crowds.

Six climbers were found dead on Mont Blanc, Europe's highest peak on Wednesday, including a British and a Dutch climber who had both been missing since July 10. Eleven other people have died on Mont Blanc since Saturday.
